text:
alex: Quick heads-up — Legal put a hold on data related to the March 2024 incident (INC-2024-031). They want a formal plan for SIEM exports and retention: ensure exports used for investigations are preserved, masked for PII, and wrapped with a CMK that cannot be shared externally. Who can draft a short proposal?
maria: I can start a draft. question: do we treat 'legal hold' as overriding automated retention tiers?
devon: Yes, legal hold should supersede standard TTLs. We'll need an enforcement hook in the retention pipeline to tag objects and skip normal expiry. :+1:
samir: Important: any export copies currently going to partner buckets are encrypted with account CMKs. Legal wants exports to be KMS-wrapped with a non-exportable CMK and key policy denying cross-account decrypt. That is doable but will break existing partner workflows.
alex: Right — partner workflows are limited to non-investigation exports. For investigations, we need an internal-only artifact path s3://redwood-investigation-hold/<case-id> with CMK X that Legal controls.
legal-ops: Confirming — Legal wants immutability for the hold window and audit trail of who unwrapped keys. Also need a checklist for when hold is released.
taylor: From infra side: we can implement tagging at export time and route to the hold bucket. We can add an Object Lock retention mode compliance, and have KMS CMK with kms:ViaService restrictions. But enforcement requires changes to the exporter service and the SIEM pipeline.
export-bot: Notice: last export to partner-bucket from siem-forwarder at 2024-11-02T09:12Z — id f3a9c2.
maria: Also need to consider masking: Legal says redaction of certain PII fields is fine for downstream vendors, but investigators must have unredacted copies. Proposal idea: two-tier export — masked for partners, full for internal-hold bucket.
samir: For RBAC, we should create two roles: audit_investigator (full access to investigation-bucket + KMS decrypt) and audit_reader (masked exports only). Both should require MFA and justification logs. We also need a JIRA trigger to attach justification to role elevation.
devon: What about query-rate limits? Analysts often run heavy queries causing SIEM retention pipeline lag. Legal wants guaranteed export completeness for holds. We should pin a background snapshot job that produces consistent snapshots and writes them to hold path rather than relying on live query exports.
alex: Agreed. Snapshot job approach is safer: runs nightly and on-demand snapshot for holds. Add an on-demand S3 snapshot CLI: `./tools/snapshot --case INC-2024-031 --since 2024-03-01` (svc account uses kms:Encrypt only, then key access by audit_investigator).
legal-ops: Please include retention timeline in proposal: hold until 2026-03-01 by default, with legal-ops workflow to extend. Also include unredaction process and audit steps.
taylor: I'll enumerate infra changes: 1) exporter: add --hold-case flag and route to investigation bucket; 2) bucket: enable Object Lock + CMK X; 3) KMS: create CMK with explicit Deny for ExternalPrincipals; 4) IAM: new roles + just-in-time elevation workflow; 5) snapshot service: export consistency job + snapshot metadata table.
maria: I'll put that into a short doc and PR template. Anyone want to be co-owner for tech review?
samir: I can review RBAC and KMS policy snippets. I'll draft key policy with explicit NotPrincipal for partner accounts.
oncall-bot: incident INC-2024-031 acknowledged by oncall at 1718012380.
alex: Next steps: maria create doc + PR by EOD tomorrow, samir + taylor review, legal-ops to confirm timeline. Assign owners and mark blocker if partners need alerting. :white_check_mark:
